docs.title: Welcome to TrackMyRupee Docs
docs.text:
TrackMyRupee is a privacy-first personal finance tracker built for India. No bank sync, no SMS access, just honest numbers from your own entries.

This guide walks you through every feature, step by step.

docs.title: Philosophy
docs.text: Understand the core design decisions and mental models behind TrackMyRupee.

docs.title: 1. Why Manual Entry, Not Bank Sync
docs.text:
TrackMyRupee does not read your SMS or connect to your bank account. You log transactions yourself.

This is a deliberate privacy-first design decision, not a missing feature. The trade-off is a few extra seconds of typing in exchange for not giving a third party read access to your bank credentials or message inbox. You stay fully in control of your data.

docs.title: 2. Why Salary Cycle, Not Calendar Month
docs.text:
Most budgeting tools reset budgets on the 1st of every month. TrackMyRupee lets you define a period that starts on your actual salary landing date (for example, the 28th) and ends the day before the next payment arrives.

This matters because your spending and saving decisions happen relative to when money arrives, not relative to the calendar. A salary-cycle budget reflects how money actually flows in your life.

docs.title: 3. Income Types: Salary vs. Passive vs. One-off
docs.text:
The app separates income into distinct source types: Salary, Freelance / Consulting, Business, Investment Returns, Rental Income, Cashback and Rewards, Refund / Reimbursement, and Other.

Mixing predictable recurring income with lumpy one-off receipts hides your true monthly run-rate. Keeping them separate gives you an honest picture of how much reliable income you actually have each cycle.

docs.title: 4. What Smart Insights and Financial Health Actually Are
docs.text:
The Financial Health score and Smart Insights panel perform descriptive pattern-matching over your own historical data. For example, they can tell you that you are spending a higher percentage on a category this cycle compared to last cycle.

They are not financial advice and are not predictions about the future. Use them as data-informed prompts for your own judgment.

docs.title: 5. Net Worth as the North Star
docs.text:
Every feature in TrackMyRupee, including budgets, loans, transfers, and capital events, ultimately feeds into your net worth number. Keeping that number accurate is the purpose of everything else in the app.

Real-world use case

Priya is a software engineer paid on the 28th who does not want to link her bank account to any app after a past data-leak concern. She earns Rs. 95,000 per month and wants to know honestly whether she can afford an Rs. 80,000 trip in March. By using manual entry and salary-cycle budgets, TrackMyRupee gives her a clear picture of her savings run-rate so she can answer that question without ever sharing bank credentials.

docs.title: Getting Started
docs.text: Set up your accounts, configure your salary cycle, and establish your financial baseline in TrackMyRupee.

docs.title: 1. First Login
docs.text:
When you open TrackMyRupee for the first time, you can choose between entering demo mode or creating a real account.

If you enter demo mode, you will see a banner at the top: "You are in Demo Mode. This is a demo with sample data for illustration." The banner has links to create a free account or exit. Demo data is temporary and does not save any changes.

docs.title: 2. Setting the Salary Cycle Start Date
docs.text:
Find the pencil icon next to "Salary cycle: 01 Aug - 31 Aug" on the Dashboard. Click it and enter the day of the month when your salary typically arrives (for example, 28).

Do this before logging any transactions. Every budget period calculation depends on this date matching how money actually flows into your account.

docs.title: 3. Creating Your First Account
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Accounts → Add on desktop, or Bottom tab → Accounts → Add on mobile.

The form works as a two-step wizard:

  1. Account Basics: Enter Account Name, Account Type, Currency, and Initial Balance.
  2. Type-specific step: Fill in fields that apply to your account type.

Use these account types as a guide:

  • Cash Wallet for physical cash you carry
  • Savings Account or Salary Account for your bank accounts
  • Demat Account or Mutual Funds for investment accounts

docs.title: 4. Setting an Accurate Opening Balance
docs.text:
The opening balance you enter becomes the base that every future net worth calculation builds on. Enter the exact real-world balance of that account on the day you set it up.

If you set an incorrect opening balance and correct it later, all historical net worth data points will change.

Create all accounts before your first transaction

Add every real-world account you own, including a Cash Wallet for physical cash, before logging your first transaction. Every expense and income entry must be attached to an account. Having them all set up from the start means your Day 1 net worth is accurate rather than artificially low.

docs.title: 5. Default Categories
docs.text:
When you sign up, three default expense categories are created automatically: Food, Shopping, and Bills. You can edit, rename, or add more categories at any time in Settings → Categories.

Real-world use case

Ananya joins TrackMyRupee for the first time. She has an HDFC Salary Account (balance: Rs. 42,000), an SBI Savings Account (balance: Rs. 1,15,000), and Rs. 3,500 cash in her wallet. She creates all three accounts before logging a single transaction, using Salary Account for HDFC, Savings Account for SBI, and Cash Wallet for physical cash. Her Day 1 net worth shows Rs. 1,60,500, which is an accurate baseline she can track against going forward.

docs.title: Accounts and Net Worth
docs.text: Manage all your assets and liabilities in one place and track your overall net worth accurately.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Accounts Page
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Accounts on desktop, or tap the Accounts tab in the bottom navigation on mobile. The page groups your accounts into asset categories such as Cash and Bank, Fixed-Income, and Investments.

The Filtered Total Balance card at the top shows the combined cash and ledger balance of all accounts matching your current filter.

Filtered Total Balance vs. Net Worth

The Filtered Total Balance shows the sum of cash and accrued deposit balances for the accounts listed. It does not include the live market value of mutual fund holdings, real estate appraisals, or the deduction of outstanding loans. The Dashboard Net Worth card gives you the complete picture.

docs.title: 2. Adding an Account
docs.text:
Click + Add next to Accounts in the sidebar on desktop, or tap + Add on the Accounts page on mobile.

The form is a two-step wizard:

  1. Account Basics: Enter Account Name, Account Type, Currency, and Initial Balance.
  2. Type-specific fields: Fill in details that apply to your account type. For example, Fixed Deposits show deposit terms and maturity date fields. Credit Cards show a credit limit field.

Click Save when done.

docs.title: 3. Account Types Reference
docs.text:
Type Use for Cash Wallet Physical cash you carry Savings Account Regular bank savings account Salary Account Bank account where your salary lands Fixed Deposit FD or RD with interest accrual Mutual Funds Mutual fund or SIP investment account Demat Account Stock trading and brokerage account NPS / PF Provident fund or pension account Credit Card Credit card (tracked as a liability) Loan Account Linked to a loan for repayment tracking Physical Asset Real estate, vehicle, or other asset Insurance Life or endowment policy

Note on Recurring Deposits (RD)

RD valuation is not treated like a single lump-sum FD from day one. Each installment accrues from its own deposit date, and only installments that were actually posted are counted. If a month is skipped, that installment is not assumed automatically.

docs.title: 4. Editing Account Details and Balance
docs.text:
Click any account row to open its detail page. Use the pencil (edit) icon to update the Account Name, Initial Balance, or any type-specific fields.

If an account no longer needs new transactions but has transaction history you want to keep, mark it Inactive instead of deleting it. Inactive accounts are hidden from transaction pickers but their full history is preserved.

Deleting vs. deactivating

Deleting an account removes the account record. Any past expenses, incomes, and transfers linked to it will lose their account reference - those transaction records stay in the system but the account field becomes blank on them. If the account has any history, deactivate it instead.

docs.title: 5. Reading Account Transaction History
docs.text:
Click any account row to open its detail page. The page shows a ledger of all credits and debits, with relative timestamps such as "3 days ago" and "7 days ago".

Click the History button at the top right of the detail page to view the full unfiltered ledger for that account.

docs.title: 6. How Net Worth Is Calculated
docs.text:
The Net Worth tile on the Dashboard sums all your active account valuations and subtracts liabilities:

  • Cash and Bank accounts: ledger balance
  • Fixed Deposits: principal plus accrued interest
  • Mutual Funds and Demat: live market value using NAV (units x current NAV)
  • Physical Assets: latest appraised valuation or acquisition cost
  • Insurance: latest surrender value
  • Credit Cards and Loans: subtracted as liabilities

Real-world use case

Before deciding whether to make a Rs. 60,000 laptop purchase, Rahul opens Accounts to check his real net worth across his HDFC Salary Account, SBI Savings Account, and Cash Wallet in one place rather than opening three separate banking apps. The Filtered Total Balance shows Rs. 1,92,000 across all three, confirming he can absorb the purchase without going below his Rs. 1,00,000 emergency reserve.

docs.title: Accrued vs Invested Balance View
docs.text:
TrackMyRupee lets you switch between two ways of viewing value for selected account types.

  • Invested: what you originally put in (baseline).
  • Accrued: what it is worth right now (interest-accrued, market-priced, or appraised current value).

docs.title: 1. Where This Toggle Applies
docs.text:
The toggle applies to account types where "invested amount" and "current value" can be meaningfully different:

  • Fixed Deposits and Recurring Deposits
  • Mutual Funds and Demat Holdings
  • Physical Assets (for example, real estate or vehicle)
  • Insurance policies with surrender-value tracking

The toggle does not apply to account types that already represent today's real value directly:

  • Cash Wallet, Savings, Salary, Current, and other liquid bank accounts: the ledger balance is already today's value.
  • Credit Cards and Short-Term Credit: these are liabilities, so there is no separate invested baseline concept.
  • Loan Accounts: this is outstanding liability tracking, not an invested-versus-accrued asset view.

docs.title: Example A: Fixed Deposit
docs.text:
Rahul opens an FD with Rs. 2,00,000 at 7.0%.

  • Invested view shows: Rs. 2,00,000
  • Accrued view (after interest accrual) might show: Rs. 2,14,860

This helps Rahul compare principal committed versus current maturity-linked value.

docs.title: Example B: Holdings Account (SIP + Market Value)
docs.text:
Meera transfers Rs. 1,00,000 into her MF account and logs holdings with total cost basis Rs. 95,000. Current market value of those holdings is Rs. 98,000.

Using TrackMyRupee's current holdings formula:

$$\text{Uninvested Cash} = \max(0, 1,00,000 - 95,000) = 5,000$$

$$\text{Accrued Value} = 98,000 + 5,000 = 1,03,000$$

  • Invested view: Rs. 95,000
  • Accrued view: Rs. 1,03,000

Real-world use case

Meera uses Invested view during monthly planning to track how much capital she has actually deployed, and switches to Accrued view on review day to see current market-linked net worth including pending uninvested cash.

docs.title: 3. Insurance-Specific Note
docs.text: For insurance accounts, if no surrender value is recorded yet, both views can show Rs. 0 by design. This avoids a misleading impression that paid premium always equals current realizable value, which is usually not true for fresh or early-stage policies.

docs.title: Investment Holdings and Mutual Fund Portfolio
docs.text: Track your mutual funds, stocks, and asset valuations in real time with automated NAV synchronization, SIP transfer tracking, and precise portfolio calculations.

docs.title: 1. Overview and Navigation
docs.text:
Access your portfolio via Sidebar → Net Worth → Holdings on desktop or via More → Holdings on mobile (URL: /holdings/).

The Holdings page provides a consolidated dashboard of all active investments across your mutual fund, investment, NPS, PF, and brokerage accounts.

docs.title: 2. How NAV Calculations and Portfolio Metrics Work
docs.text: TrackMyRupee uses a multi-tiered valuation engine to calculate your real-time investment net worth accurately.

docs.title: Valuation Resolution Order
docs.text:
For any active holding, the current unit value is resolved using the following order of priority:

  1. Live Daily NAV: Fetched automatically from official AMFI (Association of Mutual Funds in India) and MFapi.in live feeds using the fund's 6-digit AMFI scheme code.
  2. Cached NAV Fallback: If the live API is temporarily unreachable, TrackMyRupee retrieves the latest cached NAV from the local fund cache.
  3. Cost Basis Fallback: If no NAV cache exists yet (for example, a newly added holding), the valuation falls back to your purchase cost basis (Units x Average Cost).

docs.title: Formulas
docs.text:
• Holding Valuation: $$\text{Current Valuation} = \text{Units} \times \text{Latest Unit NAV}$$

  • Account Total Balance: $$\text{Cost Basis Total} = \sum \left( \text{Units}_i \times \text{Average Cost}_i \right)$$ $$\text{Uninvested Cash} = \max\left(0, \text{Ledger Balance} - \text{Cost Basis Total}\right)$$ $$\text{Total Account Balance} = \sum \left( \text{Units}_i \times \text{Latest Unit NAV}_i \right) + \text{Uninvested Cash}$$

Correction applied

Before this fix (August 2026), transferred cash could be double-counted after the related holding was logged. This has been corrected by netting uninvested cash against active holdings cost basis.

  • Total Cost Basis: $$\text{Total Invested} = \sum \left( \text{Units}_i \times \text{Average Cost}_i \right)$$

  • Unrealized Gain / Loss: $$\text{Unrealized Gain} = \text{Total Portfolio Valuation} - \text{Total Invested Cost}$$

  • Growth Return Percentage: $$\text{Gain \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Unrealized Gain}}{\text{Total Invested Cost}} \right) \times 100$$

docs.title: 3. How to Set Up Recurring Transfers for SIPs
docs.text: A Systematic Investment Plan (SIP) involves transferring a fixed amount regularly (for example, Rs. 5,000 monthly) from your primary bank account into your mutual fund account.

docs.title: Step-by-Step SIP Setup
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Add → Add Subscription (or Sidebar → Subscriptions → Add).
  2. Set Transaction Type to TRANSFER.
  3. Set Description to your SIP name (for example, "Monthly SIP - Parag Parikh Flexi Cap").
  4. Set Amount to your monthly SIP allocation (for example, 5000).
  5. Set From Account to your liquid bank account (for example, HDFC Salary Account).
  6. Set To Account to your investment account (for example, Mutual Funds / Zerodha Coin).
  7. Set Frequency to Monthly and select your SIP start date.
  8. Click Save Subscription.

How SIP transfers affect your balance

On each scheduled date, TrackMyRupee automatically logs an Internal Transfer. Money leaves your bank account and enters your Mutual Fund account as ledger cash. Net worth does not change because the money is still in your own accounts. Once you log the resulting holding, that invested portion is counted through the holding value instead of separate cash. Any amount not yet allocated to a logged holding continues to appear as pending uninvested cash.

docs.title: 4. How Holdings and Units Are Updated
docs.text: As your SIP executes or when you make lump-sum investments, your holdings update in two distinct ways.

docs.title: Updating Units and Purchase Price
docs.text:
When new units are allocated by the AMC:

  1. Go to Holdings (/holdings/) or your account detail page.
  2. Click Add Holding (or open your existing holding to update it).
  3. Enter your updated cumulative Units and updated average purchase price (Avg Cost).
  4. The system updates your cost basis immediately: $$\text{New Cost Basis} = \text{Updated Units} \times \text{New Avg Cost}$$

docs.title: Automatic Daily NAV Updates
docs.text:
• Automatic background sync: TrackMyRupee runs daily background jobs that pull updated NAVs after Indian market closing hours (approximately 11 PM IST).
  • Manual instant refresh: Click the Refresh NAV icon next to any holding row to trigger an immediate live fetch.
  • External cron integration: Set up a free cron job at cron-job.org targeting GET /api/cron/sync-nav/ with X-Cron-Secret: <YOUR_CRON_SECRET> for guaranteed daily automated syncing.

docs.title: 5. Responsive Interface Features
docs.text:
• Desktop view: Full multi-column table displaying Fund Name, Account, Units, Average Cost, Current Valuation, NAV, and action buttons.
  • Mobile view: Single-card list with touch-friendly controls. Long scheme names such as "Parag Parikh Liquid Fund - Direct Plan - Growth" wrap onto multiple lines without clipping. Tap the three-dot menu on any holding row to Refresh NAV or Delete Holding.

docs.title: Adding Expenses
docs.text: Log every outgoing payment so your budget, analytics, and net worth stay accurate.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Expense Form
docs.text:
• Desktop: Click Add in the top navbar, then select Add Expense.
  • Mobile: Tap the + button in the bottom tab bar, then tap Add Expense from the sheet that appears.

You can also use the + Add shortcut next to Expenses in the sidebar on desktop.

docs.title: 2. Using Quick Add
docs.text:
The top of the expense form has a Quick Add text box. Type a plain description such as "swiggy 320" and tap Go. The app will auto-fill the amount and suggest a category, which you can confirm or change before saving.

This is the fastest way to log an expense when you are in a hurry.

docs.title: 3. Filling the Form Manually
docs.text:
If you prefer to fill in the form yourself, complete the following fields:

  1. Amount (required): The rupee amount you spent.
  2. Category (required): The spending category, such as Food, Transport, or Bills.
  3. Description (optional): A short note about what you spent on.
  4. Account (required): The account the money came from.
  5. Date: Defaults to today. Tap More options to change it.
  6. Payment Method: Tap one of Cash, Credit Card, Debit Card, UPI, or NetBanking.

Click Save when you are done.

docs.title: 4. Where the Expense Appears
docs.text:
After saving, the expense appears in several places at once:

  • The Expenses list at /expenses/
  • The Transactions list at /transactions/
  • The Dashboard Spent tile for the current period
  • The Budget bar for the category you selected

docs.title: 5. Editing or Deleting an Expense
docs.text:
Find the expense in the Expenses list and click or tap the row to open it. Use the edit icon to open the form and change any field. Click Save to apply the changes.

To delete, use the delete (trash) icon on the expense detail screen. A confirmation prompt will appear before the record is removed.

Real-world use case

After a Swiggy delivery arrives, Meera logs it in under 15 seconds: she taps the + button, selects Add Expense, enters 450 as the amount, picks Dining Out as the category, selects HDFC Savings as the account, taps UPI as the payment method, and hits Save. She immediately sees her Dining Out budget bar move forward on the Dashboard, which reminds her how close she is to her monthly limit.

docs.title: Adding Income
docs.text: Log every payment you receive so your savings rate, analytics, and net worth stay accurate.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Income Form
docs.text:
• Desktop: Click Add in the top navbar, then select Add Income.
  • Mobile: Tap the + button in the bottom tab bar, then tap Add Income.

You can also navigate to Sidebar → Income → Add on desktop.

docs.title: 2. Choosing a Source Type
docs.text:
The Source Type field tells the app what kind of income this is. Choose the option that best describes the payment:

Source Type When to use it Salary Your regular monthly salary Freelance / Consulting Project fees or consulting payments Business Revenue from your own business Investment Returns Dividends, interest, or capital gains Rental Income Rent received from tenants Cashback and Rewards Credit card cashback or loyalty rewards Refund / Reimbursement Money returned to you (expense refund, bill reimbursement) Other Anything that does not fit the above

Why source type matters

The app separates your predictable income (Salary) from one-off receipts (Refund / Reimbursement) when calculating your savings rate. Cashback and Rewards and Refund / Reimbursement types are excluded from the savings rate denominator so they do not inflate your rate artificially.

docs.title: 3. Filling the Form
docs.text:
Complete the following fields:

  1. Date: When the money arrived.
  2. Account: Which account the money landed in.
  3. Amount: The amount received.
  4. Currency: Defaults to your profile currency.
  5. Source Type: Select from the list above.
  6. Description (optional): A short note, such as the client name or invoice number.

If this income repeats every month, toggle Mark as Recurring and select the Frequency. This creates a subscription that auto-posts the income going forward without any manual entry.

Click Save when done.

docs.title: 4. Where the Income Appears
docs.text:
After saving, the income entry appears in:

  • The Income list at /income/list/, grouped by source type
  • The Dashboard Income tile for the current period
  • The Analytics charts for year-to-date totals

docs.title: 5. Editing or Deleting an Income Entry
docs.text:
Find the entry in the Income list. Click or tap it to open the edit form. Change any field and click Save to apply the update.

To delete, use the delete action on the income detail screen and confirm the prompt.

Real-world use case

Vikram is a freelance designer. On the 1st he logs his Rs. 45,000 monthly retainer as Source Type: Freelance / Consulting and toggles Mark as Recurring with Monthly frequency, so it auto-posts every month. On the 20th he receives a one-off Rs. 10,000 project bonus and logs it manually as Freelance / Consulting without the recurring toggle. Keeping them separate means his income list clearly shows the regular retainer versus the one-off bonus, and Analytics does not treat the bonus month as his new normal.

docs.title: Recurring Transactions and Subscriptions
docs.text: Automate repeating transactions so you never miss a due date or forget to log a regular payment.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Subscription Form
docs.text:
• Desktop: Click Add in the top navbar, then select Add Subscription.
  • Mobile: Tap the + button in the bottom tab bar, then tap Add Subscription.

You can also navigate to Sidebar → Subscriptions → Add on desktop.

docs.title: 2. Filling the Three-Step Wizard
docs.text: The form is organized into three steps:

docs.title: Step 1: Basics
docs.text:
• Transaction Type: Choose Expense for bills like streaming services or phone plans, Income for a monthly retainer, Transfer for a recurring investment or SIP, or Loan Repayment for EMI payments.
  • Description: The name of the subscription (for example, "Airtel Broadband" or "Netflix").
  • Amount: The recurring amount.
  • Currency: Defaults to your profile currency.
  • Payment Method: Cash, Credit Card, Debit Card, UPI, or NetBanking.

docs.title: Step 2: Schedule
docs.text:
• Frequency: How often the transaction repeats (Monthly, Weekly, Quarterly, Yearly, or a custom interval).
  • Start Date: The date of the first occurrence.
  • End Date (optional): The date after which the subscription stops auto-posting.

docs.title: Step 3: Account and Details
docs.text:
• Account: The account to debit (for expenses) or credit (for income).

Click Save Subscription when done.

docs.title: 3. How Auto-Posting Works
docs.text: On each scheduled date, the recurring engine automatically creates a new ledger entry. You do not need to log it manually. The entry appears in your Transactions list, Expenses or Income list, and the relevant Budget bar.

docs.title: 4. The "Renewing Soon" Section
docs.text:
The Subscriptions list at /recurring/ shows a Renewing Soon section for any subscription whose next due date is within the next 30 days, sorted by days remaining. The sidebar also shows a due-soon badge when subscriptions are coming up.

This gives you advance notice before a charge hits your account.

docs.title: 5. Cancelling a Subscription
docs.text:
Find the subscription in the Subscriptions list. Tap the delete or remove action and confirm the deletion. The subscription will stop auto-posting from the next scheduled date.

There is no pause option

If you want to temporarily stop a subscription from auto-posting, delete it and recreate it when you want it to resume. There is no built-in pause feature.

Real-world use case

Sneha sets up her Rs. 1,179 per month Airtel Broadband bill once as a recurring expense: Transaction Type Expense, Description Airtel Broadband, Amount 1179, Frequency Monthly, Payment Method NetBanking, Account HDFC Salary Account. Every month the app automatically posts the expense on the due date. She never has to remember to log it. The Renewing Soon section alerts her a few days ahead so a temporarily low balance does not catch her off guard.

docs.title: Transfers
docs.text: Move money between your own accounts without double-counting it as income or an expense.

docs.title: 1. Overview
docs.text:
An Internal Transfer moves money from one account you own to another. It does not change your net worth because the money stays within your own financial ecosystem. It is excluded from your income and expense totals in Analytics and the Dashboard.

Common uses include:

  • Moving your month-end surplus from a salary account into a savings or investment account
  • Sweeping idle cash from a savings account into a mutual fund account
  • Moving physical cash into a bank account

docs.title: 2. Opening the Transfer Form
docs.text:
• Desktop: Click Add in the top navbar, then select Internal Transfer.
  • Mobile: Tap the + button in the bottom tab bar, then tap Internal Transfer.

docs.title: 3. Filling the Form
docs.text:
Complete the following fields:

  1. Amount: The amount you are moving.
  2. Date: When the transfer happens. Defaults to today.
  3. From Account: The account money leaves.
  4. To Account: The account money arrives in.
  5. Description (optional): A short note such as "Monthly savings sweep".

Click Execute Transfer to save.

docs.title: 4. What Happens After a Transfer
docs.text:
The transfer debits the From Account and credits the To Account immediately. Both account balances update the moment you click Execute Transfer.

The transfer appears in the Transactions list at /transactions/ with a special transfer indicator. It does not appear in the Expenses or Income lists.

Do not log a transfer as Expense and Income

A common mistake is logging the outflow as an expense from one account and the inflow as income to another. This double-counts the money in your Analytics, inflating both your total expense and total income figures by the transferred amount. Always use Add → Internal Transfer instead.

docs.title: 5. Setting Up Recurring Transfers for SIPs
docs.text:
For automated monthly investments such as a Systematic Investment Plan (SIP), set up a recurring Transfer rather than logging separate manual records each month:

  1. Go to Add → Add Subscription.
  2. Set Transaction Type to TRANSFER.
  3. Set From Account to your bank account (for example, HDFC Salary).
  4. Set To Account to your investment account (for example, Mutual Funds).
  5. Set Frequency to Monthly and enter your SIP amount.
  6. Click Save Subscription.

Every month, money automatically moves from your bank account balance into your Mutual Fund account's cash pool. You can then update your mutual fund holdings under Holdings and Portfolio.

Real-world use case

After checking the Trends page and finding that Rs. 80,000 has been sitting idle in his SBI Savings Account for three cycles, Arjun decides to sweep Rs. 25,000 into his Mutual Funds account each month. He sets up the transfer via Add → Internal Transfer, From Account: SBI Savings, To Account: Mutual Funds, Amount: 25,000, and clicks Execute Transfer. His Accounts page immediately shows SBI balance down by Rs. 25,000 and Mutual Funds up by Rs. 25,000. His net worth is unchanged but his asset allocation is now working harder.

docs.title: Budgets
docs.text: Set per-category monthly spending limits and get alerted before you overshoot.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Budgets Page
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Budgets on desktop, or go to More → Budgets from the mobile bottom sheet.

The page shows a Total Budget Goal bar at the top, which displays how much of your overall budget envelope has been used. Below that, individual category bars show the spend versus the limit for each category. Status pill counts at the top tell you at a glance how many categories are over budget, at their limit, on track, or have no limit set.

docs.title: 2. Setting a Category Limit
docs.text:
1. Find the category you want to limit in the list.
  2. Click the pencil (edit) icon next to the category name.
  3. Enter the monthly limit in rupees.
  4. Click Save.

The progress bar for that category updates immediately to show the new limit against your existing spend for the current period.

Categories without a limit

If a category has no limit set, it appears in the list but without a progress bar. The budget bar only activates once you set a limit.

docs.title: 3. Reading the "Needs Attention" Section
docs.text:
The Needs Attention section lists categories that are over budget (spent is more than the limit) or exactly at their limit. This is your primary action list for the current cycle.

When a category goes over budget, the bar turns red. When it reaches 90 percent or more of the limit, it turns amber as an early warning.

docs.title: 4. Adjusting a Limit Mid-Cycle
docs.text:
You can raise or lower a category limit at any time during the month. Changing the limit does not alter any past transactions. Your existing spend stays as it is; only the percentage threshold recalculates.

Use this to course-correct if a limit was set too tightly for an unusual month.

docs.title: 5. Filtering by Period
docs.text:
The Budget page has date selectors at the top. Use these to view budget adherence for a specific month or year, and to compare how a category has performed across different periods.

Real-world use case

Mid-cycle, Pooja notices her Dining Out bar has reached 210 percent of its Rs. 5,000 limit. She has two choices: raise the limit to Rs. 10,000 to match reality for this cycle (useful if she had a special occasion), or commit to cooking at home for the remaining weeks and use the budget bar as a daily check-in. She raises the limit for this cycle but uses the historical filter to verify whether last cycle's spend was also over Rs. 5,000 before deciding whether to update her default limit going forward.

docs.title: Loans
docs.text:
Track your active loans, watch repayment progress, and let the app calculate your remaining principal automatically.

Plan required

The Loans feature is available on the Plus or Pro plan. The Loans link appears in the sidebar only when your account has Plus or Pro tier active.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Loans Page
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Loans on desktop, or go to More → Loans on mobile.

Click Add to open the Add New Loan form.

docs.title: 2. Filling the Loan Form
docs.text:
Complete the following required fields:

  1. Loan Name: A short label, for example "HDFC Home Loan" or "Personal Loan Oct 2024".
  2. Loan Type: Select from the dropdown: Home Loan, Vehicle Loan, Education Loan, Personal Loan, Business Loan, Loan Against Property, or Gold Loan.
  3. Currency: Defaults to your profile currency.
  4. Principal Amount: The total amount borrowed.
  5. Interest Rate (%): The annual interest rate on the loan.
  6. Duration (Months): The total repayment tenure in months.
  7. Start Date: The date the loan was disbursed.

As you fill in the numbers, the form shows a live Estimated Monthly EMI preview at the bottom.

Click Create Loan to save.

Gold Loan and bullet-style repayment

Gold Loans (and other interest-only or bullet-style loans) behave differently from EMI amortization. During interest-only periods, principal can stay flat while only interest is paid. The full principal is then settled at maturity or final payoff.

docs.title: 3. How Repayments Are Logged
docs.text:
Loan repayments are set up as recurring transactions via Add → Add Subscription. In the subscription form, set Transaction Type to Loan Repayment and link it to the relevant loan.

Each time the recurring engine auto-posts a repayment, the remaining principal on the loan detail page decreases by the principal portion of that EMI.

docs.title: 4. Reading the Paid-Off Percentage and Remaining Balance
docs.text:
On the Loans list page, each loan card shows:

  • A paid-off percentage bar
  • The remaining principal in rupees

Click any loan card to open its detail page, which shows the full repayment history, amortization schedule, and the breakdown of principal versus interest for each payment.

docs.title: 5. What Happens When a Loan Is Fully Paid Off
docs.text:
When the remaining principal reaches zero, TrackMyRupee automatically marks the loan as closed (inactive). You do not need to do anything manually.

The closed loan stays visible in the Loans list for your records and is marked as closed. It no longer counts as a liability in your net worth.

Real-world use case

Ravi took a Rs. 1,20,000 personal loan 6 months ago to fund a travel trip. He adds it to TrackMyRupee with Principal Amount Rs. 1,20,000, Interest Rate 14 percent, Duration 12 months, and the disbursement date. The app calculates his estimated EMI at approximately Rs. 10,754 per month. Each time he makes a payment, the recurring engine auto-posts a Loan Repayment entry, and the paid-off percentage bar on the loan card ticks upward, giving him a visible motivation to make an extra prepayment and close it in 10 months instead of 12.

docs.title: Capital Events
docs.text: Record large, one-time payments without distorting your regular monthly expense analytics.

docs.title: 1. What Is a Capital Event
docs.text:
A Capital Event is a large, one-off payment that you do not want skewing your regular monthly spending charts.

Examples include a home loan down payment, a lump-sum medical bill, a car purchase, or a big renovation payment.

The rule of thumb is this: if the amount is large enough to make your average monthly expense chart look abnormal for several months, log it as a Capital Event instead of a regular expense.

docs.title: 2. What Capital Events Are Excluded From
docs.text:
Capital Events are excluded from:

  • Monthly budget calculations
  • Monthly average spend charts
  • Budget bar progress for any category

They are included in:

  • Your overall cash flow
  • Your net worth calculations (your account balance decreases correctly)

This means your Dining Out, Transport, and Groceries budget bars remain unaffected by the one-off payment, and your Analytics average monthly expense chart continues to reflect your real recurring spend.

docs.title: 3. Opening the Capital Event Form
docs.text:
• Desktop: Navigate to Sidebar → Capital Events → Add.
  • Mobile: Go to More → Capital Events → Add.

The form is titled "Add Capital Event".

docs.title: 4. Filling the Form
docs.text:
Complete the following fields:

  1. Amount (required): The total amount of the payment.
  2. Date (required): The date the payment was made.
  3. Subtype (required): The category of the capital event, such as Home Renovation, Vehicle Purchase, Medical, or Loan Prepayment.
  4. Account (optional): Link the event to an account to update its balance automatically.
  5. Linked Loan (optional): Link a down payment or prepayment to a specific loan record so it appears in that loan's history.

Click Save when done.

docs.title: 5. Linking a Capital Event to a Loan
docs.text:
If you are recording a home loan down payment or a lump-sum prepayment on an existing loan, use the Linked Loan field to connect the Capital Event to that loan record.

The loan detail page will then show the capital payment as part of the total capital committed, giving you a complete picture of your repayment history.

Real-world use case

Kavya pays a Rs. 4,00,000 home renovation advance in July. She logs it as a Capital Event with Subtype: Home Renovation, Account: HDFC Savings, Amount: 4,00,000, rather than as a regular expense. Her HDFC Savings account balance drops correctly and her net worth reflects the outflow. But her Dining Out, Groceries, and Transport budget bars are unaffected, and the Analytics average monthly expense chart for the rest of the year still shows her real recurring spend instead of a Rs. 4,00,000 spike warping every future month-over-month comparison.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text: Get a daily, colour-coded view of all your transactions and cash flow events.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Calendar
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Calendar on desktop, or go to More → Calendar on mobile (URL: /calendar/).

Use the left and right arrow buttons to step through months.

docs.title: 2. Reading the Colour Legend
docs.text:
The calendar uses colours to distinguish different types of activity on each day:

Colour label What it means Income A day when money was received Expense A day when money was spent Investments A day when an investment transfer was made Pending An upcoming scheduled transaction Salary Day The day your salary cycle starts Upcoming Sub A subscription due soon

Days with more activity appear darker on the heat scale. A day with just one small transaction will appear lighter than a day with several large ones.

docs.title: 3. Clicking Into a Day
docs.text:
Tap or click any day cell to see all transactions logged on that date. The detail view shows each transaction's amount, category, and account.

This is the fastest way to audit a specific day if you notice an unexpected balance change.

docs.title: 4. Using the Search Box
docs.text:
The Calendar page includes a search box at the top. Type a keyword such as a merchant name or a category name to highlight or filter matching entries across the month.

Real-world use case

Deepak notices an unusually dark day on the August calendar. He clicks into it and finds three separate grocery orders totalling Rs. 2,400 that he does not remember placing. He checks the descriptions and realises a household member used his account. The Calendar's day detail view gave him the full audit trail in seconds, prompting him to enable spending notifications so he is alerted the moment any transaction is logged.

docs.title: Analytics, Trends and Financial Health
docs.text: Understand your savings rate, spending patterns, and overall financial health with data-driven summaries.

docs.title: 1. Opening Analytics
docs.text: Navigate to Sidebar → Analytics on desktop, or go to More → Analytics on mobile (URL: /analytics/).

docs.title: 2. Reading the Financial Health Score
docs.text:
The Health Score card at the top of the Analytics page shows a score from 0 to 100. The score is calculated from your year-to-date (YTD) savings rate:

Score What it means Savings rate 10 Needs attention Negative (spending more than income) 40 Needs improvement 0 to 20 percent 70 (Stable) On track 20 to 30 percent 95 (Wealth Builder) Excellent 30 percent or more

Expand the Health Breakdown section to see the four component metrics that make up the score:

  • Savings Rate: The percentage of income saved year-to-date
  • Expense Growth: Your current monthly average spend compared to your 3-month historical average
  • Consistency: How many of the last 10 months had positive savings
  • Risk Buffer: Months of financial runway, calculated as YTD savings divided by average monthly expense

docs.title: 3. Understanding YTD Totals
docs.text: The Analytics page shows year-to-date totals for Income, Expenses, and Invested amounts, along with a YTD Savings Rate. These are factual summaries of the data you have logged. They are not predictions or advice.

docs.title: 4. Reading the Trends Page
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Trends on desktop, or go to More → Analytics → Trends on mobile (URL: /trends/).

The Trends page shows two key analyses:

  • Category Creep Detection: Identifies categories where your spend has grown significantly compared to a previous period. This helps you spot gradual increases before they become a problem.
  • Asset Allocation Health: Shows how your wealth is distributed across cash, fixed-income, and market-linked investments. A flag appears if too much wealth is sitting idle in low-yield accounts.

docs.title: 5. Using Year and Date Selectors
docs.text:
Both the Analytics and Trends pages have year and date range selectors at the top. Use these to:

  • Compare your current year's performance against a prior year
  • Zoom into a specific period such as a quarter or a custom date range

docs.title: 6. An Important Note on All Insights
docs.text:
The Financial Health score, the insights panel, and all Trends analyses are descriptive summaries of your own historical data. They show what has happened in your records.

They are not financial advice and they do not predict future outcomes. Use them as data-informed prompts for your own decision-making.

Real-world use case

Nisha is considering applying for a personal loan and wants to understand her financial standing first. She opens Analytics and checks her Health Score. It shows 40 (savings rate 12 percent, Needs Improvement). She then opens Trends and sees an over-idle flag: Rs. 1.8 lakh sitting in a Savings Account earning 3 percent per year. She transfers Rs. 80,000 into her Mutual Fund account via Add → Internal Transfer, which shifts her asset allocation. Two months later, with her savings rate up to 22 percent and the idle-cash flag cleared, her Health Score moves to 70 (Stable), giving her a cleaner financial picture before she approaches a lender.

docs.title: Savings Goals
docs.text:
Set a savings target, contribute funds from any account, and track progress toward your goal.

Plan required

Savings Goals are available on the Pro plan. The Goals link appears in the sidebar and in the mobile More sheet under Net Worth only when your account has the Pro tier active.

docs.title: 1. Opening the Goals Page
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Goals on desktop, or go to More → Goals on mobile.

Click Add Goal to open the goal creation form.

docs.title: 2. Creating a Goal
docs.text:
Fill in the following fields:

  1. Goal Name: A short label for what you are saving toward, for example "Goa Trip Fund", "Emergency Reserve", or "MacBook".
  2. Target Amount: The total rupee amount you want to reach.
  3. Target Date (optional): A deadline for reaching the goal. When set, the progress card will calculate how much you need to contribute per remaining salary cycle.
  4. Linked Account: The account whose balance contributions will be counted toward this goal.

Click Save.

docs.title: 3. Logging a Contribution
docs.text:
Navigate to Sidebar → Goals and find your goal card. Click Add Contribution.

Enter the amount and the source account. The contribution is recorded as a goal contribution ledger entry. It debits the source account and credits the goal, so your net worth stays accurate.

Use a dedicated savings account

Create a separate Savings Account in the app (for example, "Goa Trip Savings") and link it to the goal. Transfer your monthly contribution from your salary account to this dedicated account via Add → Internal Transfer. The goal's progress bar will reflect the transferred amount automatically.

docs.title: 4. Reading the Progress Card
docs.text:
Each goal card shows:

  • Saved so far: The total amount contributed
  • Remaining: How much more is needed to reach the target
  • Percentage complete: A visual progress bar
  • Per-cycle target: If you set a Target Date, this shows how much you need to save each salary cycle to meet the deadline

docs.title: 5. Editing or Closing a Goal
docs.text:
Click the goal card's three-dot menu to edit the goal name, target amount, target date, or linked account.

To archive a completed goal, select Mark as Completed. This does not withdraw or move any funds. It simply removes the goal from your active list and marks it as done in the records.

Real-world use case

Priya wants to save Rs. 80,000 for a Goa trip in March, which is 4 salary cycles away. She creates a goal: Goal Name: Goa Trip, Target: Rs. 80,000, Target Date: 01 Mar. The app tells her she needs to contribute Rs. 20,000 per cycle. Each time her salary arrives, she transfers Rs. 20,000 to her Goa Savings account and logs a goal contribution. The progress bar moves from 0 percent to 25 percent to 50 percent to 75 percent and finally to 100 percent, giving her a visible commitment that is harder to ignore than a mental note.

docs.title: Mobile App (iOS)
docs.text:
Install and run TrackMyRupee on your iPhone as a native app using Capacitor, which wraps the live web app.

What the mobile app is

The iOS app is a Capacitor shell that loads https://trackmyrupee.com. It uses your real account and real data in real time. It is not a separate offline app and requires an internet connection. Building it requires a Mac with Xcode.

docs.title: 1. Prerequisites
docs.text:
Before you begin, make sure you have the following installed on your Mac:

  • macOS with the latest stable Xcode (download from the Mac App Store)
  • Node.js (version 18 or later) and npm from nodejs.org
  • CocoaPods: run sudo gem install cocoapods in your terminal
  • The repository cloned locally: git clone <repository-url> && cd django-finance-tracker

docs.title: 2. Syncing Capacitor
docs.text:
Navigate to the mobile/ directory and sync the Capacitor bridge. This copies the necessary plugins and configuration into the iOS project.

cd mobile
npm install
npm run ios:sync

docs.title: 3. Opening in Xcode
docs.text:
Run the following command to open the project in Xcode automatically:

npm run ios:open

Alternatively, open mobile/ios/App/App.xcworkspace manually in Xcode. Always open the .xcworkspace file, not the .xcodeproj file.

docs.title: 4. Selecting Your Signing Team
docs.text:
1. In Xcode, click the App target in the left panel.
  2. Go to Signing and Capabilities.
  3. Under Team, select your Apple ID. A free personal team is sufficient for personal use.
  4. If Xcode shows a bundle ID conflict, change the Bundle Identifier to something unique such as com.yourname.trackmyrupee.

docs.title: 5. Building and Running
docs.text:
• Build only: Press Cmd + B
  • Run on a connected iPhone: Select your device in the top bar and press Cmd + R
  • Archive for distribution: Go to Product → Archive, then use Distribute App in the Organizer

First launch on iPhone: Untrusted Developer

When you install via a free Personal Team, iOS shows an "Untrusted Developer" error on first open. To fix it, go to Settings → General → VPN and Device Management → [your Apple ID] → Trust. Make sure your iPhone has an active internet connection during this step because it contacts Apple's servers to verify the certificate.

docs.title: 6. Free vs. Paid Development
docs.text:
Feature Free (Personal Team) Paid ($99/year Apple Developer Program) Cost Free $99 USD per year Run on your own iPhone Yes Yes App expires on device Every 7 days No App Store distribution No Yes TestFlight beta No Yes Push notifications No Yes Maximum active apps on device 3 Unlimited

For personal use on your own phone, the free option is sufficient.

docs.title: CocoaPods errors
docs.text:
cd mobile/ios/App
pod install

docs.title: "Communication with Apple failed" in Signing and Capabilities
docs.text:
1. Make sure your physical iPhone (not a simulator) is selected as the run destination in Xcode's top bar.
  2. Change the Bundle Identifier to a unique value (see step 4 above).
  3. Disable any VPN because VPNs can block Apple's signing servers.
  4. Go to Xcode → Settings → Accounts and confirm your Apple ID is listed with a valid Development certificate.

docs.title: App will not verify on iPhone
docs.text:
1. Ensure the iPhone has Wi-Fi or cellular data (not just a local network without internet access).
  2. Temporarily disable VPN, AdGuard, or custom DNS settings.
  3. Go to Settings → General → Date and Time → Set Automatically and make sure it is enabled.
  4. Delete the app from your iPhone, restart the phone, and re-run from Xcode.

Real-world use case

Ananya builds the app once on her Mac, signs it with her free Apple ID, and installs it on her iPhone. She re-runs it from Xcode every 7 days, which takes about 30 seconds, to renew the certificate. The app opens as a full-screen experience with the bottom navigation bar, identical to the browser version but without the browser chrome.

docs.title: Self-Hosting with Docker
docs.text:
Run your own private instance of TrackMyRupee on any Linux server in about 10 minutes.

Who this is for

Self-hosting gives you full data control. Your transactions never leave your server. This guide covers the Docker Compose path, which is the recommended approach. For a bare-metal Python setup without Docker, see the Manual Python Setup section below.

docs.title: 1. Clone the Repository
docs.text:
git clone <repository-url>
cd django-finance-tracker

docs.title: 2. Create Your Environment File
docs.text:
Create a file named .env in the repository root. At minimum you need the following settings:

# Required
SECRET_KEY='replace-with-a-long-random-string'
DEBUG=False

# Database (leave blank to use SQLite)
# DATABASE_URL='postgres://user:password@localhost:5432/dbname'

# Email: choose one option below

# Option A: Brevo API (recommended for self-hosting)
# BREVO_API_KEY=''

# Option B: SMTP
# EMAIL_HOST='smtp.gmail.com'
# EMAIL_PORT=587
# EMAIL_USE_TLS=True
# EMAIL_HOST_USER=''
# EMAIL_HOST_PASSWORD=''

# Optional features
# GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID=''          # Google OAuth login
# GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET=''
# RAZORPAY_KEY_ID=''           # Payments
# RAZORPAY_KEY_SECRET=''
# RAZORPAY_WEBHOOK_SECRET=''
# VAPID_PUBLIC_KEY=''          # Web Push notifications
# VAPID_PRIVATE_KEY=''
# VAPID_ADMIN_EMAIL='you@example.com'
# GEMINI_API_KEY=''            # AI category insights
# GOOGLE_ANALYTICS_ID=''
# SENTRY_DSN=''
# RECAPTCHA_PUBLIC_KEY=''
# RECAPTCHA_SECRET_KEY=''

Never commit .env to git

Your .env file contains your SECRET_KEY and any API credentials. Confirm that .env is listed in your .gitignore file before pushing any code.

docs.title: 3. Start the Containers
docs.text:
docker-compose up --build

On first start, the container automatically runs database migrations and sets up a demo user with sample data. This may take 2 to 3 minutes on first build while it downloads the base image.

docs.title: 4. Open the App
docs.text:
Navigate to http://localhost:8000 in your browser.

Sign up vs. demo

The demo user (demo / demo) is pre-populated with sample data and is read-only. Click Create Account to register your real account.

docs.title: 5. Manual Python Setup
docs.text:
If you prefer to run without Docker, follow these steps.

Requirements: Python 3.8 or later, pip

# 1. Clone
git clone <repository-url>
cd django-finance-tracker

# 2. Create a virtual environment
python3 -m venv env
source env/bin/activate   # On Windows: env\Scripts\activate

# 3. Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

# 4. Create .env (use the same variables from Step 2 above)

# 5. Run migrations
python manage.py migrate

# 6. Optional: load demo data
python manage.py setup_demo_user

# 7. Start the server
python manage.py runserver

docs.title: 6. Production Hardening Checklist
docs.text:
Before exposing your instance to the internet, complete the following steps:

  • [ ] Set DEBUG=False in .env
  • [ ] Set SECRET_KEY to a long random string (generate one with python -c "import secrets; print(secrets.token_hex(50))")
  • [ ] Put a reverse proxy such as Nginx or Caddy in front of the app for HTTPS
  • [ ] Set ALLOWED_HOSTS in settings.py or via an environment variable to your domain
  • [ ] Use PostgreSQL instead of SQLite for production by setting the DATABASE_URL variable
  • [ ] Enable email for password reset and notifications
  • [ ] Set up regular database backups

Real-world use case

Rohan runs his own instance on a Rs. 600 per month Hetzner VPS. He sets DEBUG=False, puts Caddy in front for automatic HTTPS, and points his domain finance.rohan.me at the server. His family uses the shared instance with each member having their own account, and the data never leaves their own server.

docs.title: 7. Localization
docs.text:
TrackMyRupee ships with English, Hindi, and Marathi translations. To add or update translations:

# Requires gettext
# macOS: brew install gettext
# Ubuntu: sudo apt install gettext

# Extract translatable strings
python manage.py makemessages -l mr -l hi

# Apply common financial term translations
python update_translations.py

# Compile
python manage.py compilemessages

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text: Answers to the most common questions about TrackMyRupee.

docs.title: Is TrackMyRupee free?
docs.text: TrackMyRupee has a Free plan that covers core expense tracking, budgets, and accounts. Plus and Pro plans unlock advanced features like Loans, Goals, bulk subscriptions, and email summaries. See trackmyrupee.com/#pricing for current plan details.

docs.title: Does the app connect to my bank or read my SMS?
docs.text: No. TrackMyRupee is privacy-first by design. It does not read SMS, connect to net banking APIs, or access your bank statement. You log transactions manually (or via the Quick Add text box). This is a deliberate choice. See Philosophy for the full reasoning.

docs.title: Is my data safe?
docs.text: Yes. Data is encrypted in transit (HTTPS), stored securely, and never sold to third parties. If you prefer to host your own instance, see Self-Hosting. You get full data control with zero data leaving your server.

docs.title: Can I use TrackMyRupee in currencies other than rupees?
docs.text: Yes. Each transaction and account has its own Currency field. The app supports INR, USD, EUR, GBP, and more. Set your preferred display currency in Settings → Profile.

docs.title: What happens if I delete an account?
docs.text: The account record is removed, but transactions linked to that account are not deleted. They just lose their account reference (the account field becomes blank on those records). If you want to stop using an account without losing the association, mark it inactive instead. See Accounts and Net Worth for details.

docs.title: How do I fix my opening balance?
docs.text: Go to Accounts → [your account] → Edit (pencil icon). Update the Initial Balance field and save. The change takes effect immediately and all future net worth calculations will use the corrected baseline.

docs.title: How do I handle a joint account?
docs.text: Create the account once under one user's TrackMyRupee account and log all transactions manually. There is no shared-account multi-user sync at this time.

docs.title: Why should I use "Internal Transfer" instead of logging an Expense and Income?
docs.text: A transfer moves money between accounts you already own. It does not change your net worth. Logging it as Expense and Income double-counts it, inflating both your total income and total expense figures in Analytics. Always use Add → Internal Transfer for account-to-account moves. See Transfers.

docs.title: Can I import transactions from a spreadsheet?
docs.text: Yes. The app supports .xlsx bulk upload. Your file must have columns: Date, Amount, Description, Category. During upload you select a Target Year, which overrides the year in the file. Access this via Sidebar → Expenses → Upload.

docs.title: What is a Capital Event and when should I use it?
docs.text: A Capital Event is a large, one-off payment such as a car down-payment, home renovation advance, or lump-sum medical bill that you do not want distorting your monthly average charts. It still appears in your cash flow and net worth but is excluded from budget calculations. As a rule of thumb: if the amount is large enough to make your average monthly expense chart look abnormal for months, log it as a Capital Event. See Capital Events.

docs.title: What does "auto-posting" mean for recurring transactions?
docs.text: When a recurring transaction's scheduled date arrives, the TrackMyRupee engine automatically creates a new ledger entry. You do not need to manually log it. It appears in your Transactions list, Expenses or Income list, and any relevant Budget bar. See Recurring and Subscriptions.

docs.title: My budget bar shows 0% even though I have logged expenses. Why?
docs.text: The budget bar only counts expenses in categories that have a limit set. If a category has no rupee limit, it appears in the list but without a bar. Click the pencil icon next to the category to set a limit.

docs.title: What is the Financial Health Score?
docs.text:
A score from 0 to 100 calculated from your year-to-date savings rate:

Score Label Savings rate 10 Needs attention Negative (spending exceeds income) 40 Needs improvement 0 to 20 percent 70 Stable 20 to 30 percent 95 Wealth Builder 30 percent or more

Expand the Health Breakdown section on the Analytics page to see four component metrics: Savings Rate, Expense Growth, Consistency (positive-savings months out of last 10), and Risk Buffer (months of runway). See Analytics and Health.

docs.title: Why does my savings rate feel lower than expected?
docs.text: The savings rate denominator excludes Cashback and Rewards and Refund / Reimbursement income, so one-off recoveries do not artificially inflate your rate. This gives you a truer picture of how much you are genuinely saving from your earned income.

docs.title: Why did my loan disappear or turn grey?
docs.text: When the remaining principal on a loan reaches zero, TrackMyRupee automatically marks the loan as inactive (closed). It does not disappear. It is still visible in the Loans list, just marked as closed. A closed loan no longer counts as a liability in your net worth. See Loans.

docs.title: How do I log an extra prepayment on a loan?
docs.text: Log a Capital Event with the relevant Subtype and link it to the loan via the Linked Loan field. The Loan Detail page will then show the prepayment as part of total capital committed. See Capital Events.

docs.title: Is there an Android app?
docs.text: Not currently. The iOS app (built with Capacitor) is available for personal sideloading. The web app at trackmyrupee.com is fully responsive and works well as a Progressive Web App (PWA) on Android. Add it to your home screen from Chrome for an app-like experience.

docs.title: Can I host TrackMyRupee on my own server?
docs.text: Yes. Full self-hosting is supported via Docker Compose. See Self-Hosting for the step-by-step guide.

docs.title: दर्शन (Philosophy)
docs.text: TrackMyRupee के पीछे के मुख्य डिज़ाइन निर्णयों और विचारों को समझें।

docs.title: 1. मैन्युअल प्रविष्टि क्यों, बैंक सिंक क्यों नहीं?
docs.text:
TrackMyRupee आपके SMS नहीं पढ़ता और न ही आपके बैंक खाते से जुड़ता है। आप स्वयं अपने लेनदेन लॉग करते हैं।

यह एक जानबूझकर लिया गया गोपनीयता-प्रथम डिज़ाइन निर्णय है, कोई गायब सुविधा नहीं। कुछ सेकंड टाइपिंग के बदले में किसी तीसरे पक्ष को अपने बैंक क्रेडेंशियल या मैसेज इनबॉक्स का एक्सेस न देना इसका मुख्य लाभ है। आपका डेटा पूरी तरह आपके नियंत्रण में रहता है।

docs.title: 2. वेतन चक्र (Salary Cycle) क्यों, कैलेंडर महीना क्यों नहीं?
docs.text:
अधिकांश बजट उपकरण हर महीने की 1 तारीख को बजट रीसेट करते हैं। TrackMyRupee आपको एक ऐसी अवधि परिभाषित करने देता है जो आपके वास्तविक वेतन आने की तारीख (उदाहरण के लिए 28 तारीख) से शुरू होती है और अगला वेतन आने से एक दिन पहले समाप्त होती है।

यह महत्वपूर्ण है क्योंकि आपके खर्च और बचत के फैसले इस आधार पर होते हैं कि पैसा कब आता है, न कि कैलेंडर की तारीख पर। वेतन-चक्र बजट यह दर्शाता है कि आपके जीवन में पैसा वास्तव में कैसे बहता है।

docs.title: 3. आय के प्रकार: वेतन बनाम निष्क्रिय बनाम एकमुश्त
docs.text:
ऐप आय को अलग-अलग स्रोत प्रकारों में विभाजित करता है: वेतन, फ्रीलांस / कंसल्टिंग, व्यवसाय, निवेश रिटर्न, किराया आय, कैशबैक और पुरस्कार, रिफंड / प्रतिपूर्ति, और अन्य।

नियमित वेतन को एकमुश्त आय के साथ मिलाने से आपकी वास्तविक मासिक आय छिप जाती है। इन्हें अलग रखने से आपको यह स्पष्ट चित्र मिलता है कि आपके पास हर चक्र में कितनी विश्वसनीय आय उपलब्ध है।

docs.title: 4. स्मार्ट अंतर्दृष्टि और वित्तीय स्वास्थ्य वास्तव में क्या हैं?
docs.text:
वित्तीय स्वास्थ्य स्कोर और स्मार्ट अंतर्दृष्टि पैनल आपके अपने ऐतिहासिक डेटा का विश्लेषण करते हैं। उदाहरण के लिए, वे आपको बता सकते हैं कि आप पिछले चक्र की तुलना में इस चक्र में किसी श्रेणी पर अधिक प्रतिशत खर्च कर रहे हैं।

ये वित्तीय सलाह नहीं हैं और न ही भविष्य की भविष्यवाणियां हैं। इनका उपयोग अपने निर्णय के लिए डेटा-आधारित संकेत के रूप में करें।

docs.title: 5. निवल संपत्ति (Net Worth) प्राथमिक लक्ष्य के रूप में
docs.text:
TrackMyRupee की हर सुविधा, जिसमें बजट, लोन, ट्रांसफर और कैपिटल इवेंट्स शामिल हैं, अंततः आपकी निवल संपत्ति के आंकड़े में योगदान करती है। उस आंकड़े को सटीक रखना ऐप का मुख्य उद्देश्य है।

वास्तविक उपयोग का उदाहरण

प्रिया एक सॉफ्टवेयर इंजीनियर हैं जिन्हें 28 तारीख को वेतन मिलता है। पिछले डेटा-लीक के डर से वह अपना बैंक खाता किसी ऐप से नहीं जोड़ना चाहतीं। वह प्रति माह ₹95,000 कमाती हैं और जानना चाहती हैं कि क्या वह मार्च में ₹80,000 की यात्रा का खर्च उठा सकती हैं। मैन्युअल प्रविष्टि और वेतन-चक्र बजट का उपयोग करके, TrackMyRupee उन्हें उनकी बचत दर का स्पष्ट चित्र देता है ताकि वह बैंक क्रेडेंशियल साझा किए बिना उत्तर पा सकें।

docs.title: शुरुआत करें (Getting Started)
docs.text: अपने खाते सेट करें, अपना वेतन चक्र कॉन्फ़िगर करें और TrackMyRupee में अपनी वित्तीय आधाररेखा स्थापित करें।

docs.title: 1. पहला लॉगिन
docs.text:
जब आप पहली बार TrackMyRupee खोलते हैं, तो आप डेमो मोड में प्रवेश करने या एक वास्तविक खाता बनाने के बीच चयन कर सकते हैं।

यदि आप डेमो मोड में प्रवेश करते हैं, तो आपको शीर्ष पर एक बैनर दिखाई देगा: "आप डेमो मोड में हैं। यह उदाहरण के लिए नमूना डेटा के साथ एक डेमो है।" बैनर में मुफ़्त खाता बनाने या बाहर निकलने के लिंक हैं। डेमो डेटा अस्थायी है और कोई भी बदलाव सहेजता नहीं है।

docs.title: 2. वेतन चक्र प्रारंभ तिथि सेट करना
docs.text:
डैशबोर्ड पर "Salary cycle: 01 Aug - 31 Aug" के बगल में स्थित पेंसिल आइकन खोजें। उस पर क्लिक करें और वह तारीख दर्ज करें जब आपका वेतन आमतौर पर आता है (उदाहरण के लिए 28)।

कोई भी लेन-देन दर्ज करने से पहले ऐसा करें। हर बजट अवधि की गणना इस बात पर निर्भर करती है कि यह तारीख आपके पैसे के आगमन से मेल खाती है।

docs.title: 3. अपना पहला खाता बनाना
docs.text:
डेस्कटॉप पर Sidebar → Accounts → Add पर जाएँ, या मोबाइल पर Bottom tab → Accounts → Add पर टैप करें।

फॉर्म दो-चरणीय विजार्ड के रूप में काम करता है:

  1. खाते की बुनियादी जानकारी: खाता नाम, खाता प्रकार, मुद्रा और प्रारंभिक शेष दर्ज करें।
  2. प्रकार-विशिष्ट चरण: अपने खाते के प्रकार पर लागू होने वाले फ़ील्ड भरें।

मार्गदर्शक के रूप में इन खाता प्रकारों का उपयोग करें:

  • अपने पास मौजूद नकद के लिए Cash Wallet
  • अपने बैंक खातों के लिए Savings Account या Salary Account
  • निवेश खातों के लिए Demat Account या Mutual Funds

docs.title: 4. सटीक प्रारंभिक शेष निर्धारित करना
docs.text:
आपके द्वारा दर्ज किया गया प्रारंभिक शेष वह आधार बन जाता है जिस पर हर भविष्य की निवल संपत्ति की गणना होती है। सेटअप के दिन उस खाते का सटीक वास्तविक शेष दर्ज करें।

यदि आप एक गलत प्रारंभिक शेष सेट करते हैं और बाद में इसे ठीक करते हैं, तो सभी ऐतिहासिक निवल संपत्ति डेटा बिंदु बदल जाएंगे।

अपने पहले लेन-देन से पहले सभी खाते बनाएं

अपना पहला लेन-देन लॉग करने से पहले अपने पास मौजूद हर वास्तविक खाते को जोड़ें, जिसमें नकद खर्च के लिए कैश वॉलेट भी शामिल है। प्रत्येक व्यय और आय प्रविष्टि को एक खाते से जोड़ा जाना चाहिए। शुरुआत से ही उन सभी को सेट करने का अर्थ है कि आपका Day 1 निवल संपत्ति कृत्रिम रूप से कम होने के बजाय सटीक है।

docs.title: 5. डिफ़ॉल्ट श्रेणियां
docs.text:
जब आप साइन अप करते हैं, तो तीन डिफ़ॉल्ट व्यय श्रेणियां स्वचालित रूप से बन जाती हैं: भोजन (Food), खरीदारी (Shopping), और बिल (Bills)। आप ऐप की सेटिंग्स में किसी भी समय अधिक श्रेणियों को संपादित, नाम बदल या जोड़ सकते हैं।

वास्तविक उपयोग का उदाहरण

अनन्या पहली बार TrackMyRupee से जुड़ती है। उसके पास HDFC सैलरी अकाउंट (शेष: ₹42,000), SBI सेविंग्स अकाउंट (शेष: ₹1,15,000), और उसके वॉलेट में ₹3,500 नकद हैं। वह एक भी लेन-देन लॉग करने से पहले तीनों खाते बनाती है — HDFC के लिए सैलरी अकाउंट, SBI के लिए सेविंग्स अकाउंट, और भौतिक नकद के लिए कैश वॉलेट का उपयोग करके। उसका Day 1 निवल संपत्ति ₹1,60,500 दिखाता है, जो एक सटीक आधाररेखा है।

docs.title: खाते और निवल संपत्ति (Accounts and Net Worth)
docs.text: अपनी सभी संपत्तियों और देनदारियों को एक ही स्थान पर प्रबंधित करें और अपनी कुल निवल संपत्ति को सटीक रूप से ट्रैक करें।

docs.title: 1. खाते का पृष्ठ खोलना
docs.text:
डेस्कटॉप पर Sidebar → Accounts पर जाएँ, या मोबाइल पर निचले नेविगेशन में Accounts टैब पर टैप करें। यह पृष्ठ आपके खातों को संपत्ति श्रेणियों जैसे नकद और बैंक, फिक्स्ड-इनकम और निवेश में समूहित करता है।

शीर्ष पर Filtered Total Balance कार्ड आपके वर्तमान फ़िल्टर से मेल खाने वाले सभी खातों की संयुक्त शेष राशि दिखाता है।

फ़िल्टर की गई कुल शेष राशि बनाम निवल संपत्ति

Filtered Total Balance सूचीबद्ध खातों के लिए नकद और संचित जमा शेष का योग दिखाता है। इसमें म्यूचुअल फंड होल्डिंग्स का लाइव बाजार मूल्य, अचल संपत्ति का मूल्यांकन, या बकाया ऋणों की कटौती शामिल नहीं है। डैशबोर्ड Net Worth कार्ड आपको संपूर्ण चित्र देता है।

docs.title: 2. नया खाता जोड़ना
docs.text:
डेस्कटॉप पर साइडबार में Accounts के बगल में + Add पर क्लिक करें, या मोबाइल पर Accounts पृष्ठ पर + Add पर टैप करें।

फॉर्म दो-चरणीय विजार्ड है:

  1. खाते की बुनियादी जानकारी: खाता नाम, खाता प्रकार, मुद्रा और प्रारंभिक शेष दर्ज करें।
  2. प्रकार-विशिष्ट फ़ील्ड: अपने खाते के प्रकार पर लागू होने वाले विवरण भरें। उदाहरण के लिए, फिक्स्ड डिपॉजिट जमा अवधि और परिपक्वता तिथि फ़ील्ड दिखाते हैं। क्रेडिट कार्ड क्रेडिट सीमा फ़ील्ड दिखाते हैं।

सहेजने के लिए Save पर क्लिक करें।

docs.title: 3. खाता प्रकार संदर्भ
docs.text: प्रकार उपयोग Cash Wallet आपके पास मौजूद नकद Savings Account नियमित बैंक बचत खाता Salary Account बैंक खाता जहां आपका वेतन आता है Fixed Deposit ब्याज संचय के साथ FD या RD Mutual Funds म्यूचुअल फंड या SIP निवेश खाता Demat Account स्टॉक ट्रेडिंग और ब्रोकरेज खाता NPS / PF भविष्य निधि या पेंशन खाता Credit Card क्रेडिट कार्ड (देनदारी के रूप में ट्रैक किया गया) Loan Account पुनर्भुगतान ट्रैकिंग के लिए ऋण से जुड़ा Physical Asset अचल संपत्ति, वाहन, या अन्य संपत्ति Insurance जीवन या बंदोबस्ती नीति

docs.title: 4. खाता विवरण और शेष राशि संपादित करना
docs.text:
इसके विवरण पृष्ठ को खोलने के लिए किसी भी खाते की पंक्ति पर क्लिक करें। खाता नाम, प्रारंभिक शेष, या किसी भी प्रकार-विशिष्ट फ़ील्ड को अपडेट करने के लिए पेंसिल (संपादित करें) आइकन का उपयोग करें।

यदि किसी खाते में नए लेन-देन की आवश्यकता नहीं है, लेकिन आपके पास लेन-देन का इतिहास है जिसे आप रखना चाहते हैं, तो इसे हटाने के बजाय Inactive (निष्क्रिय) के रूप में चिह्नित करें।

हटाना बनाम निष्क्रिय करना

खाता हटाने से खाता रिकॉर्ड हट जाता है। इससे जुड़े किसी भी पिछले व्यय, आय और हस्तांतरण का खाता संदर्भ समाप्त हो जाएगा। यदि खाते का कोई इतिहास है, तो इसे हटाने के बजाय निष्क्रिय करें।

docs.title: 5. खाता लेन-देन इतिहास पढ़ना
docs.text:
विवरण पृष्ठ खोलने के लिए किसी भी खाते की पंक्ति पर क्लिक करें। पृष्ठ सभी क्रेडिट और डेबिट का एक बहीखाता दिखाता है, जिसमें सापेक्ष समय-मुहरें जैसे "3 दिन पहले" शामिल हैं।

उस खाते के पूर्ण अनफ़िल्टर्ड बहीखाता देखने के लिए विवरण पृष्ठ के शीर्ष दाईं ओर History बटन पर क्लिक करें।

docs.title: 6. निवल संपत्ति की गणना कैसे की जाती है
docs.text:
डैशबोर्ड पर Net Worth टाइल आपके सभी सक्रिय खाता मूल्यांकनों को जोड़ती है और देनदारियों को घटाती है:

  • नकद और बैंक खाते: बहीखाता शेष
  • फिक्स्ड डिपॉजिट: मूलधन प्लस अर्जित ब्याज
  • म्यूचुअल फंड और डीमैट: NAV का उपयोग करके लाइव बाजार मूल्य (इकाइयां x वर्तमान NAV)
  • भौतिक संपत्तियां: नवीनतम मूल्यांकन या अधिग्रहण लागत
  • बीमा: नवीनतम अभर्पण मूल्य
  • क्रेडिट कार्ड और लोन: देनदारियों के रूप में घटाए गए

वास्तविक उपयोग का उदाहरण

₹60,000 का लैपटॉप खरीदने का फैसला करने से पहले, राहुल तीन अलग-अलग बैंकिंग ऐप खोलने के बजाय अपने HDFC सैलरी अकाउंट, SBI सेविंग्स अकाउंट और कैश वॉलेट में अपनी वास्तविक निवल संपत्ति की जांच करने के लिए Accounts खोलता है। Filtered Total Balance तीनों में ₹1,92,000 दिखाता है, जिससे पुष्टि होती है कि वह अपने ₹1,00,000 के आपातकालीन बफर से नीचे जाए बिना खरीदारी कर सकता है।

docs.title: निवेश होल्डिंग्स और म्यूचुअल फंड पोर्टफोलियो (Holdings)
docs.text: स्वचालित NAV सिंक्रनाइज़ेशन, SIP ट्रांसफर ट्रैकिंग और सटीक पोर्टफोलियो गणना के साथ वास्तविक समय में अपने म्यूचुअल फंड, स्टॉक और संपत्ति मूल्यांकन को ट्रैक करें।

docs.title: 1. अवलोकन और नेविगेशन
docs.text:
डेस्कटॉप पर Sidebar → Net Worth → Holdings के माध्यम से या मोबाइल पर More → Holdings के माध्यम से अपने पोर्टफोलियो तक पहुंचें (URL: /holdings/)।

Holdings पृष्ठ आपके म्यूचुअल फंड, निवेश, NPS, PF और ब्रोकरेज खातों में सभी सक्रिय निवेशों का एक समेकित डैशबोर्ड प्रदान करता है।

docs.title: 2. NAV गणना और पोर्टफोलियो मीट्रिक कैसे काम करते हैं
docs.text: TrackMyRupee आपकी वास्तविक समय की निवेश निवल संपत्ति की सटीक गणना करने के लिए एक बहु-स्तरीय मूल्यांकन इंजन का उपयोग करता है।

docs.title: मूल्यांकन समाधान क्रम
docs.text:
किसी भी सक्रिय होल्डिंग के लिए, वर्तमान इकाई मूल्य का समाधान प्राथमिकताओं के निम्नलिखित क्रम का उपयोग करके किया जाता है:

  1. लाइव दैनिक NAV: फंड के 6-अंकीय AMFI स्कीम कोड का उपयोग करके आधिकारिक AMFI और MFapi.in लाइव फ़ीड से स्वचालित रूप से प्राप्त किया गया।
  2. कैश्ड NAV फॉलबैक: यदि लाइव API अस्थायी रूप से पहुंच योग्य नहीं है, तो TrackMyRupee स्थानीय फंड कैश से नवीनतम कैश्ड NAV पुनर्प्राप्त करता है।
  3. लागत आधार फॉलबैक: यदि अभी तक कोई NAV कैश मौजूद नहीं है (उदाहरण के लिए, एक नई जोड़ी गई होल्डिंग), तो मूल्यांकन आपकी खरीद लागत आधार (इकाइयां x औसत लागत) पर वापस आ जाता है।

docs.title: सूत्र
docs.text:
• होल्डिंग मूल्यांकन: $$\text{Current Valuation} = \text{Units} \times \text{Latest Unit NAV}$$

  • खाता कुल शेष राशि: $$\text{Cost Basis Total} = \sum \left( \text{Units}_i \times \text{Average Cost}_i \right)$$ $$\text{Uninvested Cash} = \max\left(0, \text{Ledger Balance} - \text{Cost Basis Total}\right)$$ $$\text{Total Account Balance} = \sum \left( \text{Units}_i \times \text{Latest Unit NAV}_i \right) + \text{Uninvested Cash}$$

सुधार लागू

अगस्त 2026 से पहले, लॉग की गई होल्डिंग्स के बाद ट्रांसफर किया गया कैश दो बार गिना जा सकता था। अब यह गणना सही कर दी गई है।

  • कुल लागत आधार: $$\text{Total Invested} = \sum \left( \text{Units}_i \times \text{Average Cost}_i \right)$$

  • अप्रत्यक्ष लाभ / हानि: $$\text{Unrealized Gain} = \text{Total Portfolio Valuation} - \text{Total Invested Cost}$$

  • वृद्धि रिटर्न प्रतिशत: $$\text{Gain \%} = \left( \frac{\text{Unrealized Gain}}{\text{Total Invested Cost}} \right) \times 100$$

docs.title: 3. SIP के लिए आवर्ती हस्तांतरण कैसे सेट करें
docs.text: एक सिस्टमैटिक इन्वेस्टमेंट प्लान (SIP) में आपके प्राथमिक बैंक खाते से आपके म्यूचुअल फंड खाते में नियमित रूप से एक निश्चित राशि (उदाहरण के लिए, ₹5,000 मासिक) स्थानांतरित करना शामिल है।

docs.title: चरण-दर-चरण SIP सेटअप
docs.text:
1. Add → Add Subscription (या Sidebar → Subscriptions → Add) पर जाएं।
  2. Transaction Type को TRANSFER पर सेट करें।
  3. Description को अपने SIP नाम (उदाहरण के लिए, "Monthly SIP - Parag Parikh Flexi Cap") पर सेट करें।
  4. Amount को अपने मासिक SIP आवंटन (उदाहरण के लिए, 5000) पर सेट करें।
  5. From Account को अपने बैंक खाते (उदाहरण के लिए, HDFC Salary Account) पर सेट करें।
  6. To Account को अपने निवेश खाते (उदाहरण के लिए, Mutual Funds / Zerodha Coin) पर सेट करें।
  7. Frequency को Monthly पर सेट करें और अपनी SIP प्रारंभ तिथि चुनें।
  8. Save Subscription पर क्लिक करें।

SIP हस्तांतरण आपकी शेष राशि को कैसे प्रभावित करता है

प्रत्येक अनुसूचित तिथि पर, TrackMyRupee स्वचालित रूप से एक आंतरिक हस्तांतरण लॉग करता है। पैसा आपके बैंक खाते से निकलकर म्यूचुअल फंड खाते में लेजर कैश के रूप में आता है। आपकी कुल निवल संपत्ति तुरंत नहीं बदलती क्योंकि पैसा आपके अपने खातों में ही रहता है। जब आप संबंधित होल्डिंग लॉग करते हैं, तो वह हिस्सा अलग कैश की तरह नहीं, बल्कि होल्डिंग वैल्यू में गिना जाता है। जो राशि अभी होल्डिंग में आवंटित नहीं हुई है, वही uninvested cash के रूप में दिखती रहती है।

docs.title: 4. होल्डिंग्स और इकाइयों को कैसे अपडेट किया जाता है
docs.text: जैसे ही आपका SIP निष्पादित होता है या जब आप एकमुश्त निवेश करते हैं, तो आपकी होल्डिंग्स दो अलग-अलग तरीकों से अपडेट होती हैं।

docs.title: इकाइयाँ और खरीद मूल्य अपडेट करना
docs.text:
जब AMC द्वारा नई इकाइयाँ आवंटित की जाती हैं:

  1. Holdings (/holdings/) या अपने खाते के विवरण पृष्ठ पर जाएँ।
  2. Add Holding पर क्लिक करें (या अपडेट करने के लिए अपनी मौजूदा होल्डिंग खोलें)।
  3. अपनी अद्यतन संचयी Units और अद्यतन औसत खरीद मूल्य (Avg Cost) दर्ज करें।
  4. सिस्टम आपकी लागत के आधार को तुरंत अपडेट करता है: $$\text{New Cost Basis} = \text{Updated Units} \times \text{New Avg Cost}$$

docs.title: स्वचालित दैनिक NAV अपडेट
docs.text:
• स्वचालित बैकग्राउंड सिंक: TrackMyRupee दैनिक बैकग्राउंड जॉब चलाता है जो भारतीय बाजार बंद होने के समय (लगभग रात 11 बजे IST) के बाद अद्यतन NAV खींचता है।
  • मैनुअल इंस्टेंट रिफ्रेश: तत्काल लाइव प्राप्त करने के लिए किसी भी होल्डिंग पंक्ति के बगल में Refresh NAV आइकन पर क्लिक करें।

  • आवर्ती लेनदेन और सदस्यताएँ

docs.title: व्यय जोड़ना (Adding Expenses)
docs.text: अपने सभी खर्चों को आसानी से लॉग करें और ट्रैक करें ताकि आपका बजट, विश्लेषण और निवल संपत्ति सटीक बनी रहे।

docs.title: 1. व्यय फॉर्म खोलना
docs.text:
• डेस्कटॉप: शीर्ष नेविगेशन बार में Add पर क्लिक करें, फिर Add Expense चुनें।
  • मोबाइल: निचले टैब बार में + बटन पर टैप करें, फिर दिखाई देने वाली शीट से Add Expense पर टैप करें।

आप डेस्कटॉप पर साइडबार में Expenses के बगल में स्थित + Add शॉर्टकट का भी उपयोग कर सकते हैं।

docs.title: 2. क्विक ऐड का उपयोग करना
docs.text:
व्यय फॉर्म के शीर्ष पर एक Quick Add टेक्स्ट बॉक्स है। "swiggy 320" जैसा एक साधारण विवरण टाइप करें और Go पर टैप करें। ऐप राशि को स्वतः भर देगा और एक श्रेणी का सुझाव देगा, जिसे आप सहेजने से पहले पुष्टि या बदल सकते हैं।

जब आप जल्दी में हों तो व्यय लॉग करने का यह सबसे तेज़ तरीका है।

docs.title: 3. मैन्युअल रूप से फॉर्म भरना
docs.text:
यदि आप स्वयं फॉर्म भरना पसंद करते हैं, तो निम्नलिखित फ़ील्ड भरें:

  1. Amount (आवश्यक): आपके द्वारा खर्च की गई रुपया राशि।
  2. Category (आवश्यक): व्यय श्रेणी, जैसे भोजन (Food), परिवहन (Transport), या बिल (Bills)।
  3. Description (वैकल्पिक): आप किस पर खर्च किया, इसके बारे में एक संक्षिप्त टिप्पणी।
  4. Account (आवश्यक): वह खाता जिससे पैसा निकाला गया।
  5. Date: आज की तारीख पर सेट रहता है। इसे बदलने के लिए More options पर टैप करें।
  6. Payment Method: नकद (Cash), क्रेडिट कार्ड (Credit Card), डेबिट कार्ड (Debit Card), UPI, या नेटबैंकिंग (NetBanking) में से किसी एक पर टैप करें।

पूरा होने पर Save पर क्लिक करें।

docs.title: 4. व्यय कहाँ दिखाई देता है
docs.text:
सहेजने के बाद, व्यय एक साथ कई स्थानों पर दिखाई देता है:

  • /expenses/ पर Expenses सूची में
  • /transactions/ पर Transactions सूची में
  • वर्तमान अवधि के लिए डैशबोर्ड पर Spent टाइल पर
  • आपके द्वारा चुनी गई श्रेणी के लिए Budget बार पर

docs.title: 5. व्यय संपादित करना या हटाना
docs.text:
Expenses सूची में व्यय खोजें और इसे खोलने के लिए पंक्ति पर क्लिक या टैप करें। फॉर्म खोलने और किसी भी फ़ील्ड को बदलने के लिए संपादन आइकन का उपयोग करें। परिवर्तनों को लागू करने के लिए Save पर क्लिक करें।

हटाने के लिए, व्यय विवरण स्क्रीन पर हटाएं (कचरा पात्र) आइकन का उपयोग करें। रिकॉर्ड हटाने से पहले एक पुष्टिकरण संकेत दिखाई देगा।

वास्तविक उपयोग का उदाहरण

Swiggy डिलीवरी आने के बाद, मीरा इसे 15 सेकंड से भी कम समय में लॉग करती है: वह + बटन पर टैप करती है, Add Expense चुनती है, राशि के रूप में 450 दर्ज करती है, श्रेणी के रूप में Dining Out चुनती है, खाते के रूप में HDFC Savings चुनती है, भुगतान विधि में UPI पर टैप करती है, और Save दबाती है। वह तुरंत डैशबोर्ड पर अपने Dining Out बजट बार को आगे बढ़ते हुए देखती है, जो उसे याद दिलाता है कि वह अपनी मासिक सीमा के कितने करीब है।

docs.title: आय जोड़ना (Adding Income)
docs.text: अपनी सभी आय को लॉग करें और वर्गीकृत करें ताकि आपकी बचत दर, विश्लेषण और निवल संपत्ति सटीक रहे।

docs.title: 1. आय फॉर्म खोलना
docs.text:
• डेस्कटॉप: शीर्ष नेविगेशन बार में Add पर क्लिक करें, फिर Add Income चुनें।
  • मोबाइल: निचले टैब बार में + बटन पर टैप करें, फिर Add Income पर टैप करें।

आप डेस्कटॉप पर Sidebar → Income → Add पर भी जा सकते हैं।

docs.title: 2. स्रोत प्रकार चुनना
docs.text:
Source Type फ़ील्ड ऐप को बताता है कि यह किस प्रकार की आय है। उस विकल्प को चुनें जो भुगतान का सबसे अच्छा वर्णन करता है:

स्रोत प्रकार कब उपयोग करें Salary आपका नियमित मासिक वेतन Freelance / Consulting प्रोजेक्ट फीस या कंसल्टिंग भुगतान Business आपके अपने व्यवसाय से राजस्व Investment Returns लाभांश, ब्याज, या पूंजीगत लाभ Rental Income किरायेदारों से प्राप्त किराया Cashback and Rewards क्रेडिट कार्ड कैशबैक या पुरस्कार Refund / Reimbursement आपको वापस मिला पैसा (व्यय रिफंड, बिल प्रतिपूर्ति) Other कुछ भी जो उपरोक्त में फिट नहीं बैठता

स्रोत प्रकार क्यों मायने रखता है

आपकी बचत दर की गणना करते समय ऐप आपकी अनुमानित आय (Salary) को एकमुश्त प्राप्तियों (Refund / Reimbursement) से अलग करता है। कैशबैक और रिफंड प्रकारों को बचत दर के हर से बाहर रखा जाता है ताकि वे आपकी दर को कृत्रिम रूप से न बढ़ाएं।

docs.title: 3. फॉर्म भरना
docs.text:
निम्नलिखित फ़ील्ड भरें:

  1. Date: पैसा कब आया।
  2. Account: पैसा किस खाते में आया।
  3. Amount: प्राप्त राशि।
  4. Currency: आपकी प्रोफ़ाइल मुद्रा पर डिफ़ॉल्ट रहता है।
  5. Source Type: ऊपर दी गई सूची में से चुनें।
  6. Description (वैकल्पिक): एक संक्षिप्त टिप्पणी, जैसे ग्राहक का नाम या चालान संख्या।

यदि यह आय हर महीने दोहराई जाती है, तो Mark as Recurring को टॉगल करें और Frequency चुनें। यह एक सदस्यता बनाता है जो बिना किसी मैन्युअल प्रविष्टि के भविष्य में आय को स्वतः पोस्ट करती है।

पूरा होने पर Save पर क्लिक करें।

docs.title: 4. आय कहाँ दिखाई देती है
docs.text:
सहेजने के बाद, आय प्रविष्टि इसमें दिखाई देती है:

  • स्रोत प्रकार के आधार पर समूहीकृत /income/list/ पर Income सूची
  • वर्तमान अवधि के लिए Dashboard Income टाइल
  • वर्ष-दर-तारीख योग के लिए Analytics चार्ट

docs.title: 5. आय प्रविष्टि संपादित करना या हटाना
docs.text:
Income सूची में प्रविष्टि खोजें। संपादन फॉर्म खोलने के लिए इसे क्लिक या टैप करें। किसी भी फ़ील्ड को बदलें और अपडेट लागू करने के लिए Save पर क्लिक करें।

हटाने के लिए, आय विवरण स्क्रीन पर हटाएं कार्रवाई का उपयोग करें और पुष्टिकरण की पुष्टि करें।

वास्तविक उपयोग का उदाहरण

विक्रम एक फ्रीलांस डिज़ाइनर हैं। 1 तारीख को वह अपने ₹45,000 के मासिक रिटेनर को Source Type: Freelance / Consulting के रूप में लॉग करते हैं और Monthly आवृत्ति के साथ Mark as Recurring को टॉगल करते हैं ताकि यह हर महीने स्वतः पोस्ट हो जाए। 20 तारीख को उन्हें ₹10,000 का प्रोजेक्ट बोनस मिलता है और वह इसे आवर्ती टॉगल के बिना मैन्युअल रूप से लॉग करते हैं। इन्हें अलग रखने का अर्थ है कि उनकी आय सूची नियमित आय बनाम एकमुश्त बोनस को स्पष्ट रूप से दर्शाती है।

docs.text: दोहराए जाने वाले लेनदेन को स्वचालित करें ताकि आप कभी भी देय तिथि न चूकें या नियमित भुगतान लॉग करना न भूलें।
